findings.issue_text: Migration executes raw SQL expecting a matching SiteSetting row for 'embed_category', but since this setting defaults to '' and only changed settings are persisted, the query returns zero rows on most installs, causing [0]['id'] to raise NoMethodError on nil and crash the migration

Admin embeddable_hosts_controller's update and destroy actions fetch the record via .where(id: params[:id]).first without checking for nil, so requesting a nonexistent id raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a proper error/404
EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! unconditionally, raising NoMethodError when host is nil instead of producing a normal validation error

In store.js.es6's _hydrateEmbedded plural (_ids) branch, the raw id-array field is always deleted and replaced with the hydrated array even when _lookupSubType fails to resolve some ids, silently dropping data and leaving falsy/undefined entries, unlike the singular branch which preserves the raw field on failed lookup

New controller specs (embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb, embedding_controller_spec.rb) only assert inheritance from Admin::AdminController with no coverage of create/update/destroy/show actions, which is why the nil-host crash went undetected

Migration's backfill INSERT interpolates the legacy embeddable_hosts setting value directly into raw SQL without escaping/quoting, so a host value containing a single quote breaks or corrupts the migration

category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb have swapped contents — the former defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) and the latter defines the :category-related fabricators — so filenames no longer match their contents
The delete action's destroyRecord() call in embeddable-host.js.es6 has no .catch() handler (unlike save(), which uses popupAjaxError), so a failed host deletion fails silently with no user feedback
The saveChanges action in admin-embedding.js.es6 and its corresponding PUT /admin/customize/embedding endpoint are never invoked from any template, making it dead/unreachable code
EmbeddableHost.record_for_host performs a case-insensitive query (lower(host) = ?) with no supporting index on the host column, despite running on every embedded-comment page load and topic retrieval

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In store.js.es6's _hydrateEmbedded plural (_ids) branch, the raw id-array field is always deleted and replaced with the hydrated array even when _lookupSubType fails to resolve some ids, silently dropping data and leaving falsy/undefined entries, unlike the singular branch which preserves the raw field on failed lookup

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `_hydrateEmbedded` to support keys ending in `_ids` via `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/`. In the plural (`_ids`) branch it unconditionally does `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []; delete obj[k];` where `hydrated` is always the result of `obj[k].map(...)`. This means the original raw id array field (e.g. `category_ids`) is always deleted even if `_lookupSubType` fails to resolve some/all ids (producing `undefined`/falsy entries in the hydrated array). In contrast, the singular (`_id`) branch only deletes the raw field when hydration succeeds (`if (hydrated) { ... delete obj[k]; }`). So the finding accurately describes a correctness regression/inconsistency introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New controller specs (embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb, embedding_controller_spec.rb) only assert inheritance from Admin::AdminController with no coverage of create/update/destroy/show actions, which is why the nil-host crash went undetected

adjudication.rationale: The newly added controller specs indeed only check that Admin::EmbeddableHostsController and Admin::EmbeddingController subclass Admin::AdminController and do not exercise any controller actions (create/update/destroy/show). In the same diff, Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update and #destroy can crash if the record isn’t found (where(...).first returns nil, then save_host(nil) calls host.host=..., or host.destroy), and there is no spec coverage that would catch this scenario. The exact causality “why it went undetected” is not directly provable from the diff, but the lack of action coverage and the nil-record crash risk are both verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration's backfill INSERT interpolates the legacy embeddable_hosts setting value directly into raw SQL without escaping/quoting, so a host value containing a single quote breaks or corrupts the migration

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the backfill loop builds raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. The `h` value comes directly from the legacy `site_settings.value` for `embeddable_hosts` and is not escaped/quoted safely. If `h` contains a single quote (or other SQL-significant characters), the SQL becomes invalid (or could alter the statement), causing the migration to fail/corrupt data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The delete action's destroyRecord() call in embeddable-host.js.es6 has no .catch() handler (unlike save(), which uses popupAjaxError), so a failed host deletion fails silently with no user feedback

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... });` but does not attach a `.catch(...)` handler. In the same component, `save()` explicitly handles failures via `.catch(popupAjaxError)`. As written, if the delete request fails (network/server error), the promise rejection is unhandled here and the UI will not show the expected `popupAjaxError` feedback, so the failure can appear silent to the user.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The saveChanges action in admin-embedding.js.es6 and its corresponding PUT /admin/customize/embedding endpoint are never invoked from any template, making it dead/unreachable code

adjudication.rationale: In the added admin embedding UI, `app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines an action `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, and the backend adds a corresponding `PUT /admin/customize/embedding` route handled by `Admin::EmbeddingController#update`. However, the only new template for this page (`app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/embedding.hbs`) renders the hosts table and an "Add Host" button; it does not render any button or trigger wired to the `saveChanges` action. All persistence shown in the diff happens via `embeddable-host` component calling `host.save(props)`/`destroyRecord()`, which hits the `resources :embeddable_hosts` endpoints, not the embedding PUT endpoint. Therefore, within this diff, `saveChanges` and the PUT endpoint appear to be dead/unreachable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost.record_for_host performs a case-insensitive query (lower(host) = ?) with no supporting index on the host column, despite running on every embedded-comment page load and topic retrieval

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, which runs `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`. The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates the `embeddable_hosts` table with a `host` column but adds no index on `host` (and no functional index on `lower(host)`). The new code path calls `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` from `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, i.e., on embed requests/topic retrieval, so this becomes a potentially frequent DB lookup that will require a sequential scan as written. This is a verifiable performance defect introduced by the diff.
